source.title: How neural networks find generalizable solutions: Self-tuned annealing in deep learning

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the idea that flat minima are associated with generalizable solutions to motivate a continual-learning method, but does not measure the train-test gap described in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures an inverse relation between SGD weight variance and loss-landscape flatness, but does not test the listed claim versions' train-test generalization outcomes. Its task-1/task-2 test-error results concern catastrophic forgetting, outside the claim's stated scope.
record.test_reason: The study assumes that flat minima favor generalization, investigates SGD dynamics, and uses its findings to develop a continual-learning method. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness against train–test gaps or report comparisons testing V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report a robust inverse variance–flatness relation, develop a random-landscape explanation, and interpret SGD as self-tuned landscape-dependent annealing. They demonstrate a landscape-dependent constraint method for reducing catastrophic forgetting. Finding generalizable solutions through this mechanism is their interpretation, rather than a measured sharpness–generalization-gap result.
record.recipe_differences: Measures SGD dynamics and loss-landscape flatness, then uses the resulting insight in a continual-learning method; it does not evaluate the claim versions' generalization outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported inverse variance-flatness relation is said to hold across choices of minibatch size and learning rate, and across tested network architectures, optimization algorithms, and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight variance decreases as training-loss landscape flatness increases across diffusive PCA directions; the main experiment reports an approximate power-law exponent of four.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During the tested SGD exploration phases, weight fluctuations are smaller along flatter PCA directions.

record.problems: The reported landscape measurements do not directly assess the train-test generalization gap; numerical results for several robustness comparisons are presented in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Task-1/task-2 test-error results in Fig. 4 concern catastrophic forgetting and do not bear on the claim's same-distribution generalization versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Held-out performance comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps across networks, including comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Architecture, optimizer, and batch-size variations test robustness of the variance–flatness relation, not their effects on held-out generalization. Figure 4's continual-learning results are already declared in rows_left_out and do not test any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Large-batch generalization gaps and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the train-test gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: fully-connected neural network with two hidden layers (784 × 50 × 50 × 10)
rows.size_stated: Two hidden layers, 50 neurons each; 2,500 weights between the hidden layers.
rows.operation_detail: Measured SGD weight variance and loss-landscape flatness along principal-component directions.
rows.measure: Inverse relation between variance σi² and flatness Fi; reported power-law exponent ψ ∼ 4 for different choices of B and α.
rows.value: σi² ∼ Fi−ψ, with ψ ∼ 4 for different choices of B and α.
rows.locator: Section III, Fig. 2D; Supplementary Material Section III, Fig. S3
rows.note: This reports variance versus landscape flatness, not magnitude-aware sharpness versus the train-test gap.
rows.check: The inverse variance–flatness relation is observed, but cannot establish any listed version. Flatness is measured along PCA directions using training-loss profiles, without weight-magnitude scaling or a comparison with generalization gaps. The approximately four power-law exponent belongs to the main MNIST experiment; supplementary robustness results establish inverse dependence without establishing that exponent in every setting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
